name: add-retry
diff:
--- a/net.py
+++ b/net.py
+for _ in range(3):
+    try: return fetch()
+    except TimeoutError: continue

good: It retries fetch up to three times on timeout.
A loop keeps it simple and bounded without extra dependencies.
A slow server could make calls take triple the time.
wrong: It makes fetch faster by caching results.
To save memory on the heap.
Nothing at all can break here.

name: fix-offbyone
diff:
--- a/p.py
+++ b/p.py
-for i in range(len(xs)-1):
+for i in range(len(xs)):

good: It now visits the last element of the list too.
An empty list is fine but code indexing i+1 would overflow.
wrong: It skips the first element of the list.
Because recursion is faster than loops.
The import statement might fail on startup.

good: It adds a dry-run option that defaults to false.
store_true needs no value so usage is just the flag.
Callers must actually honour the flag or it silently does nothing.
wrong: It deletes the parser object entirely.
Flags must always take integer values.
The database schema could be corrupted.
